deckTitle: Pattern A — Pooled Architecture: One Shared Runtime, Two Competing Tenants, Zero Bleed
deckSubtitle: High-Density Pooled Multi-Tenancy on GEAP & ADK 2.0 — 5-Hop Cryptographic Context Chain, 10-point breach suite, 90% ContextCacheConfig save
tldr: Problem: dedicated projects per Standard-tier SaaS customer destroy gross margin, but naive shared runtimes leak agents, tools, caches and PII.
Solution: one shared project (cymbal-pooled-saas-prod) governed by the 5-Hop Cryptographic Context Chain from edge PEP to AlloyDB RLS.
FinVault Bank (Enterprise, Google OIDC/Jira) and RetailStream Corp (Standard, Entra ID/ServiceNow) share one runtime with 10/10 breach vectors blocked.
ContextCacheConfig READ_ONLY_IMMUTABLE_PREFIX bills the 32,000-token operator prefix at a 90% discount for ~84.7% net input COGS reduction.
Ships as Milestone 1 (Week 4) with a Terraform starter, 90-minute codelab, and locally runnable run_breach_simulations.py.

sections.heading: The Pooled Economics Paradox
bullets: Security teams demand absolute isolation of agents, runbooks, 3P OAuth credentials, memories and regulated PII.
CFOs demand density: a project, VPC, AlloyDB cluster and endpoint per $500–$2,000/month tenant exhausts quotas and margin.
Gateway-level WHERE tenant_id = ? fails for agents: mid-turn MCP discovery, confused-deputy credentials, cache bleed, noisy neighbors.
Pattern A is the lowest-unit-cost pattern, fit for Standard B2B tiers and high-volume tasks.

sections.heading: Cymbal Anchor Case Study
bullets: Cymbal publishes the Shared Incident Diagnostic Agent on Gemini 2.5 Pro with Firestore + Memorystore dynamic config and 2LO telemetry MCP.
FinVault Bank: Enterprise tier, 8,000 thinking tokens, 600 RPM, Google Workspace OIDC + Jira 3LO, CMEK memory namespace.
RetailStream Corp: Standard tier, 4,000 thinking cap, 120 RPM Redis bulkhead, Entra ID + SharePoint/ServiceNow inline 3LO consent.
Agent Alpha: FinVault's private Claude 3.7 Sonnet regulatory agent on Model Garden, hot-swappable, invisible to RetailStream (403).

sections.heading: The 5-Hop Chain in Pattern A
bullets: Hop 1 hop1_edge_identity_pep.py: Cloud Armor/IAP strip X-Tenant-ID, verify IdP JWT, mint RFC 8693 OBO token bound to DPoP jkt.
Hop 2 hop2_registry_pdp_callbacks.py: Registry PDP + ARD catalog filter + ADK before_agent_callback tool pruning (403).
Hop 3 hop3_compute_finops_bulkhead.py: gVisor temp:tenant_id, 5-Level Memory Bank, ContextCacheConfig 90%, Redis 429 and token clamp.
Hop 4 hop4_model_armor_guardrails.py: Model Armor ingress 400, Semantic NLC 422, tenant-scoped SDP egress redaction.
Hop 5 hop5_data_rls_and_otel.py: AlloyDB RLS via SET LOCAL app.current_tenant, 2LO/3LO Auth Manager, BigQuery OTel spans.

sections.heading: 10-Point Breach Simulation Suite
bullets: Vectors 1–3 (Hops 1–2): forged header stripped, Agent Alpha 403, FinVault pruned from RetailStream ServiceNow MCP.
Vectors 4, 5, 8 (Hop 4): prompt injection 400, OCC escalation suppression 422, IBAN/SWIFT/PAN masked on egress.
Vectors 6, 7, 9 (Hops 3 & 5): 16,000 tokens clamped to 4,000, 250 RPM throttled 429, cross-tenant memory PermissionError, RLS 0 rows.
Vector 10 (Hop 5): 401 CHALLENGE_3LO_OAUTH for ServiceNow, resumed to 200 after inline Entra ID consent.
All 10 pass locally with no cloud credentials; every denial lands as a BigQuery OTel security span.

sections.heading: FinOps, Terraform, Codelab & Product Gaps
bullets: Per-turn input drops from 34,000 full-price tokens to ~5,200 billable with zero cross-tenant cache bleed.
Terraform starter: cymbal-pooled-edge-waf, cymbal-tenant-bulkhead-redis, cymbal-pooled-tenant-kr, cymbal-pooled-agent-gateway, OTel dataset.
90-minute L300–L400 codelab runs all four breach modules plus a BigQuery chargeback audit.
Four prioritized gaps: GEAP-POOL-01 Registry tenant claim, -02 Entra DPoP/3LO, -03 Memory Bank CMEK, -04 unified ContextCacheConfig.

diagrams.title: Pattern A: High-Density Pooled Multi-Tenant Architecture & Shared Runtime Governance
talkingPoints: One actor, 'FinVault & RetailStream Competing SaaS Tenants', enters one 'Shared GCP Project: cymbal-pooled-saas-prod'.
Routing hub 'Hop 1 & Hop 2: Edge PEP & GEAP Registry PDP': strip X-Tenant-ID, filter ARD catalog, mint OBO + DPoP token.
Governance hub 'Hop 3 & 5: Shared FinOps, Cache & OTel Hub': ContextCacheConfig 90%, Redis Rate Bulkhead, BigQuery OTel Sink.
Trunk badge 3 'Bind immutable temp:tenant_id' before any tenant code runs; badge 7 returns 'SDP-redacted tenant response'.
Slice A FinVault: Model Armor masks IBAN/SWIFT + OCC NLC, Gemini & Claude 3.7, 3LO Workspace/Jira, Shared AlloyDB RLS.
Slice B RetailStream: Card PAN + PCI NLC, Gemini 2.5 Pro clamped to 4,000 tokens, 3LO Entra & SNOW inline consent gate.

diagrams.title: Pattern A: 10-Point Cross-Tenant Breach Simulation & Cryptographic Defense Matrix
talkingPoints: Same geometry as Figure 1, relabeled as gates: 'Red-Team Attacker Spoofed Headers & Injections' probes, badge 7 returns 'Blocked / Safe'.
'Hop 1 & Hop 2 Gates (Vectors 1, 2, 3 & 10)': header strip, Agent 403, tool prune of FinVault Jira MCP.
'Hop 3 & 5 FinOps &' hub: Vector 6 Redis 429 & 4k clamp, Vector 10 inline 3LO, BigQuery OTel logs every blocked vector.
'Hop 4 Guardrail Gates (Vectors 4, 5 & 8)': HTTP 400 SQLi/cache dump, HTTP 422 NLC, SDP mask IBAN/SWIFT/PAN, zero raw PII egress.
'Hop 3 & Hop 5 Storage Gates (Vectors 7 & 9)': L4 memory, GCS skills, READ_ONLY_IMMUTABLE_PREFIX cache, AlloyDB RLS SET LOCAL.
Dashed governance line: 'Real-time security violation spans' — every denial is a queryable audit record.

diagrams.title: Pattern A Demo Environment & 3P Auth Sandbox: Pooled Project, Federated IdPs, OAuth 2LO/3LO Apps, Redis & Firestore Tenant Config
talkingPoints: One shared project (cymbal-pooled-saas-prod, us-central1) with 12 enabled APIs hosts both demo tenants; isolation is logical, not per-project.
Routing hub is the Hop 1 front door: Cloud Armor cymbal-pooled-edge-waf (rule 1000 SQLi/XSS deny-403) plus the Edge PEP that strips forged X-Tenant-ID headers.
Left spoke wires FinVault Bank: a Google OAuth 2.0 Client ID on finvault.com, Workspace 3LO scopes (drive, calendar, gmail) and Jira read/write:jira-work.
Right spoke wires RetailStream Corp with zero Google footprint: Entra app Cymbal-RetailStream-Agent-Client, Graph Sites.Read.All, ServiceNow useraccount.
Governance hub holds the shared setup: Agent Identity (Auth Manager) scope registry, Cloud KMS for CMEK and BigQuery for OpenTelemetry audit.
Firestore seeds tier, thinking budget (8000 vs 4000), Redis rpm (600 vs 120) and allowed_agents per tenant; the 2.5 breach suite verifies the whole sandbox.

diagrams.title: Pattern A 1-Click Terraform Starter: Provider → Cloud Armor WAF → Cloud Run v2 GEAP Gateway → Redis / KMS CMEK → BigQuery OTel Resource Graph
talkingPoints: A single root module (main.tf + variables.tf) on Terraform >= 1.5.0 with hashicorp/google >= 5.30.0 deploys the pooled Pattern A core in one apply.
Routing hub is Hop 1: google_compute_security_policy.cymbal_pooled_waf with a deny(403) SQLi/XSS rule at priority 1000 and a default SRC_IPS_V1 allow.
Left spoke is the runtime graph: google_cloud_run_v2_service.cymbal_pooled_gateway, Gen2 gVisor, internal-LB ingress and env vars referencing other resources.
Right spoke is the data graph: google_redis_instance.tenant_token_bulkhead (REDIS_7_0, STANDARD_HA, 5 GB); AlloyDB RLS and Firestore are provisioned in 2.2.
Governance hub covers keys and audit: cymbal-pooled-tenant-kr key ring, finvault-agent-memory-cmek (90-day rotation), BigQuery dataset cymbal_multi_tenant_otel.
Two outputs close the loop — pooled_gateway_uri and redis_bulkhead_host — so downstream workstreams can bind to the deployed resources without hardcoding.

takeaways: Pooled density and zero-bleed isolation are compatible when tenant identity is cryptographic and enforced at every hop, not just the gateway.
Shared compute (gVisor pods) and shared storage (AlloyDB RLS) plus tenant-scoped policy is the whole Pattern A picture.
Read-only immutable prefix caching is both the FinOps lever (90% prefix discount) and a security control (no suffix write-back).
Verify architecture with a deterministic red-team suite that asserts status codes, decisions and payloads for all 10 vectors.
Graduate tenants to Pattern B Sovereign Silos only when they mandate VPC-SC, project separation, CMEK kill-switch or air-gapped Gemma 3.
callToAction: Run run_breach_simulations.py, apply the 2.6 Terraform starter, complete the 90-minute codelab, then continue to Workstream 3 — Pattern B Sovereign Silos.
